facts.text: Hillsboro was named for early settlers Valentia Hill and his brothers, who first arrived in the area beginning in 1850.
Hillsboro is located along the West Branch of the Baraboo River in Vernon County, Wisconsin.
Early settlers Albert Field, Edward Klopfleisch, and Otto Hammer helped bring newcomers and investors to Hillsboro during the mid-1800s.
The countryside surrounding Hillsboro features some of the finest round barns in the region, built by Alga Shivers.
Hillsboro once supported a diverse business landscape that produced everything from bowling pins and fertilizer to cement products and lumber.
Hillsboro's historical business landscape included a brewery that produced specialty beers known as Hillsboro Pale and Bohemian Club.
